known.title: Classify generated files before loading their contents

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a new or upgraded client runs Forge on a Debian 12 self-hosted runner using its packaged Git.
`git check-attr --source` was introduced in Git 2.40, while Debian 12 packages Git 2.39.5. With that Git, checking any nonempty set of committed paths raises an error, so ordinary closes and the affected process-ceiling tests fail. The previous index-based check worked on this version; `docs/start.md:28` and `:45` require Git to be installed but specify no newer minimum. See the [Git 2.40 release notes](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.40.0/Documentation/RelNotes/2.40.0.txt) and the [Debian package](https://packages.debian.org/bookworm/git).
findings.title: Preserve compatibility with Git 2.39

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Scale
Case: normal use - a repository regenerates 200 tracked JSON snapshots of 5 MB each and closes the change.
This call loads both versions of every text file before checking their `linguist-generated` attributes. `repo.py:167-169` retains the byte dictionary while decoding the text, so this example requires roughly 4 GB for those inputs alone, causing severe swapping or termination on a memory-limited runner. Previously, marked files were classified first and their blobs were skipped. The existing large-folder test deletes its files, so it does not exercise this added memory cost.
findings.title: Classify generated files before loading their contents

why: Main is red: the 1728 fix (ecd8d670d) added a generated-file check (src/forge/repo.py:379, read-tree HEAD and check-attr linguist-generated) that starts a second git cat-file --batch reader during every close, so tests/test_git_process_ceiling.py's three close cases fail (2 readers where 1 is allowed); the merge's related-test selection did not pick that test
